raw_response:
I’m only managing 5 mu, so I can watch the cotton closely, but I still won’t spend carelessly. Cotton has been my main crop for years, and at my age I don’t chase fancy changes unless I see a clear benefit. I have well water, so drought risk is manageable, but pumping costs money, and with just two people in the household I need a plan that is steady and not too labor-heavy. I’ll stay with cotton on all 5 mu, plant in the usual mid-April window once the soil warms, and use a locally available improved variety that has performed reliably here. I prefer a moderate input plan: enough fertilizer to protect yield, but not excessive, because on such a small farm every yuan I put into inputs has to come back.

For fertilizer, I’ll apply most of it as base fertilizer before planting, then add a smaller topdressing around squaring or early flowering if the plants look strong enough to justify it. Cotton can’t be starved early, but too much nitrogen also pushes rank growth and can delay boll setting, so I aim for a balanced rate, not the highest possible one. Since I have well irrigation, I’ll likely irrigate twice, once after establishment if moisture is short and once around flowering-boll setting if rainfall is not enough. Weed control matters early, so I’ll use herbicide and do some hand work if needed. Insects are always something to watch in cotton, so I’ll keep insecticide available but spray based on what I actually see in the field. At my age and with only two people at home, I want the crop kept clean and stable rather than trying to squeeze out the last bit of yield.
